newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Audit Chamber ending Rosgosstrakh check.
newsitem.headline: Russia Audit Chamber ending Rosgosstrakh check.

text.p: Russia's independent Audit Chamber is likely to finish its analysis of a privatisation scheme for leading insurer Rosgosstrakh by March 14, a chamber official said on Tuesday.

"Any decision by the Audit Chamber must be approved by its collegium, which is likely to happen by the end of the week," Sergei Burkov, deputy head of the chamber inspectorate reviewing the plan, told Reuters.

The State Duma lower house of parliament, worried that the assets of Rosgosstrakh, Russia's largest insurer, were undervalued, ordered the chamber to report on the results of its evaluation before March 10.
The Russian Federal Property Fund has said it would sell 50 percent of Rosgosstrakh at a cash auction this year.
Rosgosstrakh employees have subscribed for 20 percent of the remainder and will have a priority right to buy the final 30 percent.
Burkov said the International Monetary Fund had demanded that Rosgosstrakh be privatised during 1997.
But the Moscow Arbitration Court suspended the privatisation at the end of February pending a suit by a union representing state savings bank Sberbank depositors arguing they had outstanding claims.
It suspended the privatisation until March 25, when it plans to make a final ruling on the case.
